scores.rationale: None of the snippets directly address hypoxia or dissolved oxygen (DO) lethality across taxa. The corpus is dominated by DEBtox survival modeling for chemical toxicity (NEC, killing rate, LC50/time-dependence). Snippet [16] comes closest by noting that the pattern of toxic effects in time differs between chemicals and that a single standardized exposure time cannot be applied across organisms, which is loosely analogous to the idea that lethal level and time vary—but it concerns chemicals, not DO, and taxa-specific standardized exposure times reflect organism differences only tangentially. No snippet provides specific evidence about DO lethal thresholds or times differing across taxa, and none contradicts the fact. Evidence is therefore weak and essentially insufficient to confirm the hypoxia-specific stylized fact.

The closest tangential references (snippet 11 on zones of lethality and thermal lethal limits, snippets 13/18 on acute lethality test durations) discuss lethality or test methods generally but say nothing about dissolved oxygen or interspecific differences in DO tolerance. Therefore the corpus offers no real support or contradiction, and evidence is sparse/insufficient.
